transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Um, yeah… thanks. I guess it’s not anything dramatic, but I’ve been noticing at work that in longer sales strategy meetings, I keep finding reasons to get up when everyone else is staying seated. Like I’ll refill my water, or walk over by the printer for a minute, even though I know I’m supposed to just sit and participate. It’s probably not a huge deal, but it’s been happening enough that I thought maybe I should ask about it.
When you’re sitting in those meetings, do you feel physically restless?

Yeah… I think so. I wouldn’t say it’s, like, unbearable or anything, but I do get this antsy feeling sitting there for a long time. And then I’ll kind of find a “reasonable” excuse to get up, like refilling my water or walking over near the printer for a minute, even though I know I’m really supposed to stay seated and be part of the meeting. Does that make sense?
When you get up during those meetings, is it because you feel driven to do it to relieve anxiety or a nagging thought?

Not really like a scary thought or anything, no. I don’t think it’s anxiety exactly. It’s more like… I just get uncomfortable staying seated that long, and then I make it seem reasonable, like, “Oh, I’ll just refill my water,” or I’ll walk by the printer for a minute. I know I’m supposed to stay in the meeting, so I try not to make it obvious. Does that answer what you mean?
Did you have this same kind of hard time staying seated when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, because I did okay in school, but I remember it starting pretty early, definitely before high school. In elementary school my teachers would write things like I was bright, but I rushed through work, talked out of turn, forgot homework, and my desk was kind of… stuffed with half-finished papers. So, yes, I guess there was some version of it back then too.
Do you currently have trouble staying focused on tasks at work?

Yeah, somewhat. I mean, I do get my work done, so I don’t want to overstate it, but in longer strategy meetings or when I’m reading a client brief, I’ll start out paying attention and then a few minutes later realize I’ve just been staring at the same slide or paragraph. Like, I don’t actually know what the last point was. It’s embarrassing, but it happens. Does that count as what you mean?
Do these same problems with focus or restlessness happen outside of work too?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really tracked it as much outside of work, I guess because it feels less obvious or there aren’t as many consequences. I don’t want to say no if I’m just not noticing it, but nothing specific is coming to mind right away. What kind of situations do you mean?
Outside of work, do these focus or restlessness problems ever cause problems in your daily life?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, probably sometimes, but I can’t think of a clear example where it’s caused a real problem outside of work. At home it’s more like… if I’m unfocused, I can usually just come back to things later, so it doesn’t stand out as much. I don’t want to overstate it. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
At home, do you often leave tasks half-finished?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say it’s constant, but it does happen. Like I’ll get most of a proposal or a CRM update done, and then somehow leave off the very last step — sending the final version, or logging the follow-up — even though I really did mean to finish it. It feels kind of silly because it’s usually not the hard part. Is that what you mean by half-finished?
Outside of work, have these attention or unfinished-task problems ever caused a real problem for you?

I don’t know that I can point to a real problem, honestly. Outside of work it’s usually more annoying than consequential, if that makes sense. Like I might leave something and come back to it later, but I’m not sure I’d call it causing trouble. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is.
Have these attention or restlessness issues ever caused a clear problem in your relationships?

Not really, no… at least not that I can clearly point to. I mean, I’m sure I can be a little distracted sometimes, like anyone, but I don’t think it’s caused a definite relationship problem. If someone close to me were bothered, I’d want to know, but nothing specific is coming to mind. Is that helpful?
At home, do these attention problems ever make it hard for you to manage everyday responsibilities?

I’m not sure I’d say it makes it hard, exactly. At home I usually manage the basic stuff well enough. I might be a little scattered or have to remind myself to come back to something, but I don’t think there’s a clear everyday responsibility that I’m dropping because of it. At least nothing major is coming to mind. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Outside of work, do these attention or restlessness symptoms cause problems in any other setting?

I don’t think so, no. Outside of work, I’m having a hard time thinking of a setting where it’s caused an actual problem. Maybe little annoyances here and there, but nothing I’d want to overstate. If there’s a type of situation you mean, I can think about that more.
Have these attention or restlessness symptoms ever caused a clear problem for you in school?

Yeah… school is probably where I can point to it more clearly, though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was. I did well enough, but I remember it starting way before high school. In elementary school, teachers would write things like I was bright, but I rushed through work, talked out of turn, forgot homework, and my desk was kind of packed with half-finished papers. So… yes, I guess there were some clear issues there. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Before age 12, did these attention or restlessness problems cause clear trouble for you in more than one setting, like both at school and at home?

I’m a little less sure about the “more than one setting” part. I can definitely remember it at school, way before high school—like in elementary school, teachers would say I was bright but rushed, talked out of turn, forgot homework, and my desk had all these half-finished papers stuffed in it. At home, I don’t have as clear a memory of it being a big problem, so I don’t want to overstate that. Does that make sense?
Before age 12, did your parents ever complain that you were inattentive, forgetful, or constantly on the go at home?

I honestly don’t really remember my parents complaining about that in a clear way. They may have nudged me about normal kid stuff, but I can’t point to them saying I was especially forgetful or always on the go at home. I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure.
Before age 12, did you often leave chores or other tasks half-finished at home?

I’m not totally sure from before 12, honestly. I don’t have a strong memory of specific chores at home. The pattern I know I still do now is more like… I’ll get most of a proposal or a CRM update done, but then somehow leave off the last little step, like sending the final version or logging the follow-up, even though I meant to finish it. So that kind of thing fits me, but I don’t want to pretend I clearly remember it with childhood chores if I don’t.
When you’re doing something at home that requires sitting still, do you often feel antsy enough that you get up even when you meant to stay seated?

Yeah… I mean, at home it’s maybe less obvious, but the thing that actually made me come in is that in long sales strategy meetings, I keep getting up when I know I’m supposed to stay seated. I’ll tell myself I’m just refilling my water or walking over by the printer for a second, so it doesn’t look disruptive, but honestly I think I’m doing it because I feel antsy. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Outside of work, do these attention or restlessness symptoms cause a clear problem for you in any other setting?

I’m not sure I can point to a clear problem outside of work, honestly. I mean, I’m sure I have normal moments at home where I’m a little scattered or restless, but nothing that feels as obvious or concerning as what happens in meetings. I don’t want to overstate it if that makes sense.
Have these attention or restlessness symptoms caused a clear problem for you while driving?

I don’t think so, no. At least, nothing clear that I’d want to call a problem. I mean, driving is something I try to be careful about, and I haven’t noticed the same kind of issue there. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have these attention or restlessness symptoms ever caused a clear problem for you in social situations?

I don’t think so… not in a clear way. Like, socially I might sometimes feel a little restless or mentally wander, but I can’t think of it causing an actual problem with friends or anything. I wouldn’t want to make it sound bigger than it is.
